He also claimed NATO would not invoke Article 5 to defend the country as that would mean a “global catastrophe.” by Kyiv Post | Sept. 11, 2026, 10:30 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Russia’s former President Dmitry Medvedev in Moscow on March 21, 2023. (Photo by Sergei KARPUKHIN / SPUTNIK / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Dmitry Medvedev, former president and current deputy chairman of the Russian Security Council, said Lithuania would “disappear from the map of the world” if it lifts its longstanding nuclear weapons ban. Medvedev made the remarks on Friday, Sept. 11, after Russia had already threatened Vilnius earlier that same day. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . The country’s parliamentary parties had agreed to the constitutional amendments in July, while the parliamentary Committee on Legal Affairs voted 7-2 on the proposal on Wednesday, paving the way for a final decision early next year. “Lithuania, as I understand it, talked about opening the door for the possible placement of any weapon, including nuclear weapons,” Medvedev said, according to Clash Report . Advertisement “If God forbid, something like this happens and we have to react to their actions, no one will step in for them,” he continued, adding that NATO would not invoke Article 5 to defend the country as this would mean “a global catastrophe.” Simultaneously, he denied the threat of Russia attacking Europe, despite an increase in Russia’s provocations, including hybrid threats and frequent drone violations of NATO’s airspace . Advancing nuclear ban repeal despite growing threats The lifting of the ban would essentially allow NATO to deploy its nuclear forces on Lithuania’s territory. “The geopolitical situation is getting worse,” Lithuania’s President Gitanas Nauseda told reporters following the meeting with parliament party leaders, in which 50 MPs submitted an amendment to change the law . “Our constitution was written when geopolitical circumstances were totally different,” he continued. Other Topics of Interest Russian Strikes Kill 6, Injure 33 in Nationwide Barrage on Ukraine Drones, artillery and aerial bombs struck the Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk and Kirovohrad regions on Friday, killing six and injuring dozens. The move came as Finland decided to lift its own ban just a month earlier, allowing NATO to host and transport nuclear weapons on its territory in crisis situations. Lithuania remains one of Ukraine’s strongest backers in Europe, and it borders Russia’s exclave of Kaliningrad to the west and Moscow’s ally Belarus to the south. Advertisement In June 2023, Russia began deploying nuclear weapons to Belarus. The two countries conducted a joint nuclear war drill in May, centering on use of nuclear weapons and nuclear support operations. Although Belarus continues positioning itself as neutral in Russia’s war against Ukraine, it remains its ally, providing territory and critical components Russia needs for weapons making. In December 2025, Russia deployed its nuclear-capable Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missile (IRBM) to Belarus, whose combat use in Ukraine marked the first such use of its kind in history. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA London Man shot dead at London memorial service in ‘senseless act of violence’ Forty-year-old victim declared dead at the scene in East Acton in a ‘senseless act of violence’ Nadeem Badshah Sat 3 Oct 2026 18.04 EDT Last modified on Sat 3 Oct 2026 18.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a “senseless act of violence” during a memorial service in west London , police have said. Police were called on Friday at 7.47pm after multiple shots were heard in East Acton. Officers attended alongside the London ambulance service. The victim was treated at the scene on the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street, however, he was pronounced dead. The Metropolitan police said about 40 to 50 people were at the scene, including children. The man’s family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers. A postmortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force added. No arrests have been made. DCI Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence. “We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated. “We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward. “If you were around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 6pm and 8pm, please think carefully about what you saw. Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously or vehicles being driven at speed? “We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media.” Explore more on these topics London Crime Police Gun crime news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

Into Europe With $94M Purchase By Kevin Costelloe September 28, 2026 50 Facebook Twitter Linkedin Email Print Walker Precision provides Karman with European base Karman Space & Defense has purchased Walker Precision Engineering of the U.K. for about $94 million, strengthening Karman’s position in tactical missile and air defense subsystems and establishing a foothold in the European defense market. Karman Chief Executive Officer Jon Rambeau said the purchase will help with the “rising focus on regional security in Europe.” President Donald Trump has been robustly pushing the Europeans to take charge of their own defense. Karman (NYSE: KRMN) is one of a growing number of Southern California companies aiming to help the U.S. and allied war-fighting capabilities. They include Costa Mesa-based Anduril Industries, Ducommun in Santa Ana, Boeing in Seal Beach and Huntington Beach-based Mach Industries. Karman, also based in Surf City, is a supplier of components for the space and defense industries to over 80 prime contractors supporting more than 130 space and defense programs. Military, Aerospace Systems Karman’s mission-critical products include components for military and aerospace systems, protection shielding for payloads sent into outer space and propulsion systems for military use. Its customers include Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin and NASA. Karman also serves an array of commercial space and aerospace customers. In addition to the Huntington Beach headquarters, Karman has multiple facilities across the U.S. A “significant portion” of its revenue is generated from contracts with the United States military. Karman reported second quarter revenue of $182.1 million, up 58% year-over-year. Still the company’s shares have been hard-hit in recent months. They were trading at $36.21 each as of Sept. 21, close to a 52-week low, for a market cap of $4.8 billion. Walker Precison Brings Engineering, Materials Expertise Walker has operations in Scotland, England and Poland. Its advanced products support missile seekers, guidance systems and control systems on more than 25 EU tactical missile, air and defense programs for prime contractors. The company focuses on advanced capabilities spanning engineering, materials design, precision machining, electroplating and electromechanical assemblies. Karman announced the completion of the acquisition on Sept. 1. It is called Karman Space & Defense, Europe. The acquisition accelerates Karman’s expansion beyond the United States, providing a European footprint from which to add to its 17 locations across eight U.S. states. CEO Rambeau previously held top executive positions at defense giants Lockheed Martin and L3Harris Technologies, where he most recently served as president of L3’s $8 billion Communications & Spectrum Dominance segment. He succeeded Tony Koblinski as CEO in March. Want more from the best local business newspaper in the country?
